chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Maghrib is when the disk [of the sun] disappears. If you see it after that, and you have already prayed, you repeat the prayer, your fast is valid, and you refrain from eating, provided you have consumed something from it [during the time of doubt].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Maghrib prayer and fasting if one prays or eats before the sun has fully set?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for the period of *shakk* (doubt) between sunset and the complete disappearance of the sun's disk, a critical juncture for breaking the fast. It establishes that if one prays Maghrib during this ambiguous time, the prayer is valid but must be repeated as *qada* once the sun fully sets, while the fast remains intact even if food was consumed during the uncertainty. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and distinguishes between the validity of the act and the timing of its completion.
